position_a: Use region versus track with a controlled reversible test: Duplicate one region to a new independent track and compare a region edit with a track plug-in change.
position_b: Prefer region automation, separate track, or Bounce in Place for a unique treatment when it better matches the actual object, signal path, or musical problem.
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the region edit affecting only that item while the track processor affects everything on its channel strip; reject the approach if expecting one region to have an independent instrument or deleting/moving the wrong object.

position_a: Use audio region versus underlying audio file with a controlled reversible test: Duplicate an audio region, trim the duplicate nondestructively, and confirm the full source remains in the Project Audio Browser.
position_b: Prefer create a new audio file with Bounce in Place or edit a copied file destructively when it better matches the actual object, signal path, or musical problem.
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the duplicate playing a different section while the source file remains intact; reject the approach if using destructive Audio File Editor/Optimize/Delete File commands or assuming a region is the file itself.

position_a: Use midi region versus software instrument with a controlled reversible test: Duplicate the region to a new track with duplicate settings, choose a different instrument there, and compare against changing the original shared channel strip.
position_b: Prefer program-change events, articulation/key switches, or bounce the unique region to audio when it better matches the actual object, signal path, or musical problem.
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by only the new track using the alternate instrument while the original regions retain their sound; reject the approach if expecting one region on the same track to host a different instrument or creating unintended shared-channel behavior.

position_a: Use duplicate track settings versus copying content with a controlled reversible test: Duplicate a track, leave it empty, then Option-drag one region and verify that processing is independent from the original channel strip.
position_b: Prefer new track with same channel, track alternative, or region alias when it better matches the actual object, signal path, or musical problem.
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the copied part playing through its own duplicated settings without modifying the original; reject the approach if using New Track with Same Channel instead and accidentally sharing the channel strip.

position_a: Use multiple tracks using one channel strip with a controlled reversible test: Create a second track with the same channel strip in a Project Alternative and test mute/region organization versus a shared plug-in change.
position_b: Prefer duplicate settings for independent processing or use Track Alternatives when it better matches the actual object, signal path, or musical problem.
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by separate arrangement lanes feeding one shared sound and mix path; reject the approach if assuming the tracks are independent, double-triggering overlapping regions, or confusing track mute behavior.

position_a: Use copied regions and independence with a controlled reversible test: Copy one region, edit a region parameter or MIDI note in the copy, and verify whether the original changes.
position_b: Prefer MIDI alias for linked repetition or Bounce in Place for a new audio file when it better matches the actual object, signal path, or musical problem.
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the copy behaving independently at the region/event level while shared track processing remains shared; reject the approach if assuming audio waveform edits create a new file or confusing a copy with an alias/loop.

position_a: Use midi aliases versus independent copies with a controlled reversible test: Create one alias and one ordinary copy from a duplicate MIDI region, edit the parent note, and compare both.
position_b: Prefer loops, ordinary copies, Track Alternatives, or pattern regions when it better matches the actual object, signal path, or musical problem.
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the alias following the parent while the ordinary copy stays independent; reject the approach if editing the parent unintentionally, orphaning aliases, or assuming region parameters and event content share the same linkage.

position_a: Use audio region copies, clones, and loops with a controlled reversible test: Create a normal copy and a repeated clone/loop in a test track, change a safe region parameter, and inspect source-file references.
position_b: Prefer Bounce in Place to create a distinct rendered audio file when it better matches the actual object, signal path, or musical problem.
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the intended repetitions behaving as expected without creating or deleting source audio; reject the approach if assuming visual copies are new files or editing a shared source destructively.

position_a: Use region parameters versus track parameters with a controlled reversible test: Duplicate the region, change one obvious region parameter, then compare it with a track/channel-strip change.
position_b: Prefer separate track, region automation, or event-level MIDI edit when it better matches the actual object, signal path, or musical problem.
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by only the selected region changing in the first test and all regions on the track changing in the second; reject the approach if editing with multiple regions selected or confusing region gain with track fader/automation.

position_a: Use deleting a region versus deleting the recording file with a controlled reversible test: In a project copy, delete one region from the Tracks area, verify the file remains in Project Audio, then undo.
position_b: Prefer mute/hide the region, move it to an archive track, or save a Project Alternative when it better matches the actual object, signal path, or musical problem.
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the arrangement item disappearing while the source file remains recoverable; reject the approach if confirming file deletion, using Optimize File, or affecting another project that shares the file.

position_a: Use destructive versus nondestructive editing in logic with a controlled reversible test: Copy the project and source file, perform one region-level edit, and compare it with the clearly labeled file-level operation without saving the destructive test.
position_b: Prefer Bounce to a new file, duplicate the source, or consolidate project assets first when it better matches the actual object, signal path, or musical problem.
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the distinction between playback/reference changes and source-file changes becoming obvious; reject the approach if assuming Undo will always restore an external/destructively edited file or optimizing shared media.
